narrative:
Based on your application, the model has determined that you represent a 54% probability of being a bad credit risk, which unfortunately led to the denial of your loan. This decision was not made lightly, and it is based on a careful analysis of your financial profile compared to other applicants.

The most significant factor in this decision was your credit history. You have no credits or all previous credits fully paid off, which is a very rare profile among approved applicants—only about 2.3% of them share this background. While having no credit history might seem neutral, the model sees it as a risk because it lacks evidence of how you manage debt over time. This pushed the prediction strongly toward a "bad credit risk" classification.

The second most important factor was the status of your checking account, which currently has a balance between 0 and 200 Deutsche Marks. Among approved applicants, about 23% have a similar balance, but the model views this as a moderate risk because it suggests limited financial cushion. This also contributed to the negative decision.

Interestingly, your property status—owning real estate—actually worked in your favor. This is a positive factor that pushed the prediction slightly toward "good credit," as about 31% of approved applicants own real estate. However, it was not enough to overcome the stronger negative influences from your credit history and checking account.

Other aspects of your application, such as your short employment duration of less than one year and your housing situation (renting), also align with patterns seen in higher-risk applicants. For example, only 15.6% of approved applicants have been employed for less than a year, and just 15.3% rent their homes.

To improve your chances in the future, consider building a stronger credit history by taking out a small, manageable loan and repaying it on time. Additionally, increasing your savings and maintaining a higher checking account balance will demonstrate financial stability. Finally, staying in your current job for a longer period and potentially securing a guarantor could further strengthen your application.
